subject.title: [Bug]: Terminal provider model_not_available in subagent announce path can trigger chat.history storm and gateway event-loop starvation

question: Should this issue be handled as one combined runtime-stability fix, or split into provider classification, subagent parent-wake, config validation, and watchdog follow-ups?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses provider semantics, subagent delivery, current config acceptance, and gateway availability; automation should not choose which public compatibility or recovery behavior becomes the product contract.

options.title: Bound runtime first
options.body: Classify terminal model-unavailable errors and bound announce/history amplification now, while keeping config hard-fail and watchdog recovery as separately reviewed follow-ups.

options.title: Fold into existing canonicals
options.body: Treat provider classification under this issue as diagnostic context and move remaining work to the open parent-wake and config-validation issues if maintainers decide no unique chain remains.

options.title: Design a broader stability project
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one larger provider-validation, announce-delivery, and gateway-watchdog recovery design.

recommendation.title: Bound runtime first
recommendation.body: Classify terminal model-unavailable errors and bound announce/history amplification now, while keeping config hard-fail and watchdog recovery as separately reviewed follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history signal spans both subagent announce delivery and failover/runtime boundaries, which are the surfaces needing the product split decision.
